name: Anysphere (Cursor)
monetization: Sells the Cursor AI code editor via individual and enterprise subscriptions; the fastest-growing software company ever measured, now agreed to be acquired by SpaceX/xAI for $60B (pending close).
description_md: Anysphere makes Cursor, the AI-native code editor that became the emblem of the AI coding boom: ARR went from ~$1B (Nov 2025) to ~$2B (Feb 2026) to ~$4B (May–Jun 2026), with 50,000+ enterprise customers and developers at roughly two-thirds of the Fortune 500. Priced at $29.3B in its November 2025 round, it agreed in June 2026 to be acquired by SpaceX (the merged xAI/SpaceX entity) for $60B in stock — the largest acquisition of a VC-backed startup ever. **Status: acquisition pending**, expected to close Q3 2026 subject to regulatory approvals.
ai_monetization_md: Subscription revenue (Pro/Ultra individual tiers and enterprise seats) plus usage-based pricing for frontier-model consumption inside the editor. The ~$4B ARR (mid-2026) was reached faster than any software company on record, but gross margin is structurally squeezed: Cursor pays OpenAI/Anthropic for the models that generate most of its value, which motivated its in-house Composer models. Enterprise mix (reported >$1B of the ARR) is the durable part; individual-developer revenue is exposed to bundled competitors (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Gemini).
ai_strategy_md: Own the developer workflow surface while renting intelligence: ship the best AI-native editing UX, arbitrage whichever frontier model is best, and gradually verticalize with in-house models to recover margin. The SpaceX/xAI deal trades independence for distribution and compute — each Anysphere share converts to SpaceX Class A stock (ratio set by SPCX's 7-day VWAP before close), giving shareholders public-market liquidity and giving the Musk complex a flagship AI revenue stream to point at.
risk_notes_md: Acquisition-pending: the $60B is all-stock and unclosed — consideration value floats with SPCX's price, and regulatory review or market breaks could still reprice or derail it (record as committed, not realized). Model-supplier dependency: its largest costs flow to Anthropic/OpenAI, who ship competing coding agents. ARR figures are press-reported, not audited, and the census's own mid-2026 survey carried a stale lower range ($2–3B) — growth this fast makes any point estimate short-lived.

observations.notes: $2.3B Series D priced Nov 2025 at $29.3B post (widely reported; investors incl. Coatue, Accel, Nvidia, Google). Last competitive private mark before the acquisition agreement.
